lines: Take {gift_item}. I was saving it for a very good reason I forgot.
Here, {gift_item}. It feels like the sort of thing a friend should have.
Take {gift_item}. It is not much, but it is given with care.
Here is {gift_item}. You earned more than a quick thank-you.
Keep {gift_item} close. A useful gift should not need a speech.
I saved {gift_item} for someone who would actually use it.
This {gift_item} is yours. Fair help deserves fair thanks.
Take {gift_item} before I find another chore for it.
I hope {gift_item} makes the next hard day easier.
The village remembers who helps. Today it remembers with {gift_item}.
I carried {gift_item} over before work distracted me again.
Use {gift_item} well and we will call the exchange square.
{gift_item} should help more in your pack than it did on my shelf.
I chose {gift_item} because you have a habit of making useful things last.
Here. {gift_item} belongs with someone who leaves the village better than they found it.
Take {gift_item}. I remembered your help before I remembered another use for it.
This is not payment. {gift_item} is simply yours now.
I kept {gift_item} safe until I could hand it over properly.
You showed up when it mattered. Take {gift_item}.
A plain thank-you felt too small, so I brought {gift_item}.
See? {tested_villager} liked {gift_item}. I am occasionally brilliant by accident.
Ha! {gift_item} worked. I will be unbearable about this for at least a minute.
Good. {gift_item} suited {tested_villager}. I like advice that holds up.
I saw {tested_villager} smile at {gift_item}. That answers the question.
Good instinct. {gift_item} suited {tested_villager}.
That {gift_item} found the right hands.
You can stop worrying. {tested_villager} liked {gift_item}.
Remember that reaction next time you shop for {tested_villager}.
The timing helped as much as {gift_item} itself.
{tested_villager} found a use for {gift_item} right away.
You made {tested_villager} feel noticed with {gift_item}.
Trust that instinct if you choose for {tested_villager} again.
{gift_item} was still with {tested_villager} the last time I looked.
You chose something {tested_villager} wanted without making them ask.
That gift did more good than either of us expected.
{tested_villager} found a place for {gift_item} immediately.
I heard {tested_villager} mention {gift_item} twice afterward.
The smile came before the thank-you. That is usually the honest part.
You matched the gift to the person instead of the price.
{tested_villager} treated {gift_item} like it mattered.
Oh. Then pretend I said {alternative_gift}. For {gift_subject}, that sounds much wiser.
{gift_item} failed? Strange. Try {alternative_gift}. My second guesses are famous to me.
{gift_item} missed the mark for {gift_subject}. Try {alternative_gift} instead.
For {gift_subject}, bring {alternative_gift} next time and let us quietly retire my first idea.
{gift_item} sat in their hands like it had arrived at the wrong house.
I guessed badly. It happens more when I guess with confidence.
Keep {gift_item} for somebody else. {alternative_gift} has a better chance here.
That gift landed with a tiny thud. Try {alternative_gift}.
I thought {gift_subject} would like {gift_item}. My thought has apologized.
The polite smile after {gift_item} did not reach very far.
Let us write down {alternative_gift} before I improve it into another mistake.
The good news is we now know one thing not to give {gift_subject}.
{gift_item} was a poor fit. I should have asked instead of admiring my own idea.
Try {alternative_gift}. It seems less likely to make the room go quiet.
I saw where {gift_item} ended up. Let us not discuss the shelf of unwanted things.
For the next attempt, choose {alternative_gift} and a smaller audience.
{gift_subject} deserved a better guess. {alternative_gift} is mine.
I mistook my enthusiasm for knowledge again.
Take {gift_item} back before it becomes part of the furniture.
The gift did not land, but at least the mistake taught us gently.
That was advice? I thought we were guessing. Guess {alternative_gift} next.
Set {gift_item} aside and try {alternative_gift}. This advice should land better.
They did not say much about {gift_item}, which somehow said plenty.
Try {alternative_gift}, but perhaps ask from the doorway first.
Keep {gift_item}. I do not think anyone wants a second encounter.
I am stepping out of the next gift decision. You may take {alternative_gift} with you.
That went badly in a very quiet way.
They looked at {gift_item}, then at us, then toward the exit.
Bring {alternative_gift} if you must try again. I will be somewhere less visible.
I told you my advice was wobbly. It has now fallen over.
They did not enjoy {gift_item}. Please do not tell them the idea began with me.
Set {gift_item} aside. It seems to have made the room colder.
I think {alternative_gift} is safer, but my confidence is hiding.
You can apologize. I will nod from behind you.
We learned something. I wish we had learned it before the gift.
{gift_item} should go back in the pack before anybody asks questions.
If you bring {alternative_gift}, do it on a calmer day.
The room went still enough to make me remember another appointment.
Leave them alone for a bit, then ask about {alternative_gift}.
The next idea needs fewer guesses and more listening.
You tried it anyway? Bold. I respect that almost enough to suggest {alternative_gift}.
Then we correct the guess. {alternative_gift} next time.
They hated {gift_item}. Even I understood that face.
Bring {alternative_gift} next time and leave your clever speech at home.
Nobody asked for {gift_item}. Your confidence did.
Do not hand {gift_item} over again unless you want the same answer louder.
That was not bad luck. That was a bad choice wearing ribbon.
One look from them and somehow I felt scolded too.
Try {alternative_gift}. Better yet, ask first.
Keep {gift_item}. It has caused enough trouble in other hands.
You cannot force gratitude by standing there longer.
A person is not a chest you fill with random objects.
Take the hint. It could not have been larger.
If {alternative_gift} fails too, stop guessing and start listening.
{gift_item} missed the mark because you threw the idea with your eyes closed.
I gave uncertain advice. You turned it into a determined mistake.
Leave them alone until they stop looking for somewhere to put {gift_item}.
An apology will help more than explaining why the gift should have worked.
Effort does not excuse ignoring what someone actually likes.
Bring {alternative_gift} only if you have learned something since the first attempt.
